question: What did the United States and China agree in their 2025 trade truce?

report.answer_text:
The United States and China agreed to temporarily roll back tariffs, first for 90 days in May 2025 and then for about a year under a broader deal in October. Neither agreement eliminated all tariffs. (whitehouse.gov)
May 12, 2025 — Geneva. Starting May 14, the U.S. cut its recently imposed tariffs on most Chinese goods from 145% to 30%, and China cut its retaliatory tariffs on most U.S. goods from 125% to 10%. The U.S. rate still included a 20% fentanyl-related tariff, and older duties remained in place. China also agreed to suspend or remove certain non-tariff countermeasures, and both sides agreed to keep negotiating. They extended the pause for another 90 days in August. (whitehouse.gov)
October 30, 2025 — Busan. Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping agreed to keep the higher tariffs on hold for about a year. The U.S. cut its fentanyl-related tariff from 20% to 10%, while China agreed to cooperate on curbing shipments of chemicals used to make fentanyl, suspend new rare-earth export controls for a year, and resume buying U.S. soybeans and other farm products. The White House said China committed to buying at least 12 million metric tons of U.S. soybeans in the last two months of 2025 and 25 million metric tons annually from 2026 through 2028. Both sides also agreed to pause certain shipping-related measures. (govinfo.gov)
